assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Volt
items.clue: Name of the unit equal to 1 J C⁻¹.

items.label: Electric potential energy
items.clue: External work needed to assemble a set of charges from infinitely far apart.

items.label: Test charge
items.clue: Probe placed at P to sample V; its own size and sign do not affect the value.

items.label: Scalar
items.clue: Kind of quantity with a sign but no direction, so several values add as plain numbers.

questions.stem: As 60 C of charge passes through a small electric fan, 360 J of energy is transferred from electrical energy to other forms in the fan. What is the potential difference across the fan?
questions.explanation: |ΔV| = |ΔU_E|/q = 360 J ÷ 60 C = 6.0 J/C = 6.0 V. Each coulomb gives up 6.0 J in the fan.

questions.stem: An electron is released from rest at a location where the electric potential is 50 V. Moving under the electric force alone, it reaches a location where the electric potential is 250 V. How much kinetic energy has it gained? Use e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
Four small particles, each with charge +q, are held at the corners of a square of side s. What is the total electric potential energy of the system of four particles? (k = 1/(4πε₀).)

Two horizontal parallel plates, 2.5 cm apart in a vacuum, have a potential difference of 150 V between them. What is the magnitude of the acceleration of an electron between the plates? Gravity is negligible. Take e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg.

Arc 1 is a semicircular arc of radius R with charge Q spread uniformly along it; the electric potential at its center is V₁. Arc 2 is a quarter-circle arc of radius R/2 with charge Q/2 spread uniformly along it; the electric potential at its center is V₂. What is V₂/V₁?

A very long, straight line of charge has uniform linear charge density λ > 0. Point a is a perpendicular distance r_a from the line and point b is a perpendicular distance r_b from it, with r_b > r_a. What is the potential difference V_b − V_a?
Predict first. A cell has an emf of 1.5 V. What does this mean?

options.text: The cell holds a store of 1.5 C of charge, which it releases into the circuit.
The cell pushes each coulomb of charge around the circuit with a force of 1.5 N.
For each coulomb passing through the cell, 1.5 J is transferred to electrical energy.
The cell drives a current of 1.5 A through any circuit connected to it.

questions.stem: System X consists of two protons, and system Y consists of a proton and an electron. In each system an external force moves the two particles farther apart. For which system or systems does the electric potential energy increase?

options.text: Only for system Y, the proton and electron
Only for system X, the pair of protons
For both systems, as the particles separate
For neither system, since U_E falls as r grows

questions.stem: A proton and an electron are each released from rest beside one plate of a pair of oppositely charged parallel plates in vacuum: the proton beside the positive plate and the electron beside the negative plate. Each moves under the electric force alone to the opposite plate. Which particle arrives with the greater speed, and why?

options.text: Neither: charges of equal magnitude give them equal final speeds.
The electron: both gain equal kinetic energy, and its mass is smaller.
The proton: the electron moves to higher potential, raising its U_E.
The electron: its larger acceleration gives it more kinetic energy.

questions.stem: A proton (charge +e, mass m) and an alpha particle (charge +2e, mass 4m) each start from rest and are accelerated by the electric force alone through the same potential difference. What is the ratio of the alpha particle's final kinetic energy K_α to the proton's final kinetic energy K_p?

A thin rod of length L carries a uniform linear charge density λ and lies along the x-axis from x = −L/2 to x = +L/2. Point P is on the rod's perpendicular bisector, a distance y from its midpoint. Which integral gives the electric potential at P? (k = 1/(4πε₀).)

options.text: V = ∫ kλ dx/(x² + y²), from −L/2 to L/2
V = ∫ kλy dx/√(x² + y²)³, from −L/2 to L/2
V = ∫ kλ dx/√(x² + y²), from −L/2 to L/2

questions.stem: In a region of space, the electric potential depends only on the distance r from a fixed point: V(r) = β/r², where β is a positive constant. What is the electric field at distance r?

options.text: β/r³, directed away from the point
β/r, directed away from the point

questions.explanation: E_r = −dV/dr = −(−2β/r³) = +2β/r³: positive, so outward, down the potential slope.
